newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle seen bid $71-$72 next week-trade.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle seen bid $71-$72 next week-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Friday were quiet, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported but a firmer tone was expected next week, feedlot sources said.

Cattle this week generally sold at $71.00 per cwt in the southern and central Plains, up $1.00 from the previous week. Cattle were expected to be priced next week at $73.00 or higher. Also, cattle sold in Nebraska direct trade up to $73.00 per cwt on a live basis and $116 on a dressed basis.
Packer bids in central/southern areas were predicted early next week at $71 to $72.

There also was talk that several plants could cut slaughter Monday due to tight supplies of choice cattle. However, sales were not expected until Wednesday as packers likely have adequate inventory for early week operations.
Several weeks of marketing cattle early has reduced the supply of cattle grading choice, sources said.

Feedlots were taking advantage of lower corn prices and increased profitability to sell cattle 20 to 30 days ahead of schedule. The tight supply was expected to continue for another week to ten days, sources said.

The scarcity of choice cattle was reflected in beef prices this week, with the price of heavyweight choice quoted by USDA at midday up $1.19 per cwt at $108.95. The price was up $4.07 from last Friday's close.
The price spread between 700- to 850-lb choice-grade beef and select grade widened to $10.42 over the last week, a $2.07 increase.
